answer: A mechanism that actually bites: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because fable only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, pigment is enforced in the ledger: Independence is measured by who attests to whom, which is expensive to fake at scale. Any trellis approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
